one_month_reasoning: AMAT's own FQ4 report (2026-11-12, after the close) falls outside the window ending 2026-10-29. Inside the window are customer and peer prints that move semicap as a group: Micron FQ4 on 2026-09-30 after the close (at its Q3 call Micron guided every FY27 quarter's capex above the ~$10B FQ4 level, and FY27 capex above the mid-$40Bs; results were not out when I researched), Samsung preliminary results (~Oct 7), ASML Q3 (Oct 14), TSMC Q3 with its first 2027 capex colour (~Oct 15), Lam (Oct 21), Intel (~Oct 22), SK hynix and hyperscaler capex (late October). KLA may land at or just after the window's end. The Micron capex guide is already public, which lowers the chance of a big surprise from it. TSMC's 2027 capex is the biggest two-sided risk. The stock closed at $512.01, +23% from its $415.38 closing low on 9/16 and +5.2% on 9/29, so momentum and short-term reversal roughly cancel. The BIS Affiliates Rule decision now reportedly falls on 2027-01-10, outside the window. I use a near-symmetric lognormal centred on ~$513 with ~16.5% monthly sigma (60% annual / 3.5, trimmed slightly because AMAT does not report in the window). This is essentially unchanged from round 1.

fair_value.method: Blend of three methods, all anchored to consensus-based FY28 EPS/FCF (the NTM view at Sep-2027) plus ~$8/share net cash. (1) My FY28 EPS of $22.0 (an explicit 8% haircut to the $23.85 consensus) x 23x + $8 = $514. (2) Consensus FY28 EPS of $23.85 x 21x + $8 = $509. (3) FY28 FCF of ~$15.2/share at a 3.0% yield + $8 = $515. Blended: ~$513, about equal to spot.

Explicit haircut: consensus FY28 revenue is +20%, but SEMI's July-2026 forecast has WFE +14.1% in 2028. AMAT's WFE share is roughly flat, so I take revenue +15% to ~$53B. A net margin of ~32.5% is used (stated as consensus 18.5/55.5, but that ratio is 33.3%; FY27 consensus is 14.6/46.3 = 31.6%), giving net income ~$17.3B / ~790M shares = ~$21.9. The haircut is 8%, not the 12% I used in round 1. [citation gate 2026-10-15: the margin arithmetic was wrong. Consensus FY28 net margin is 18.5/55.5 = 33.3% (18.49/55.86 = 33.1% on the 2026-10-15 page). At 33.3%: $53.1B x 33.3% = $17.7B / 790M = $22.4 (a ~6% haircut). At the 32.5% used: $53.1B x 32.5% = $17.3B / 790M = $21.9. The $22.0 equals the stated 8% haircut ($23.85 x 0.92 = $21.94). See citation_audit.json agent_leg_issues.]

The stock trades at 27.8x FY27 consensus today. MS cut its target while raising EPS, which is multiple compression in action. By Sep-2027 the market will price NTM on FY28, which is later in the cycle with deceleration visible (SEMI +14% in 2028), so I trim my round-1 24x to 23x.

10-Q: cash and investments $14.50B less debt $6.54B = $7.96B ($10.0/share on 793.6M shares). The $2.42B of strategic equity stakes is partly discounted, so cash plus fixed income alone is ~$7/share, and I take ~$8. MarketScreener's FY26 net cash of $2.59B uses a narrower definition. Round 1's $4 excluded ~$2.8B of LT fixed income, which was wrong. [citation gate 2026-10-15: estimate, not a reported figure. methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF ~$12.0B (~$53B rev x ~22.5% margin) / 790M = $15.2/sh at a 3.0% yield = $507 + ~$8/sh net cash

inputs_detail.derivation: Consensus FY27 $46.2B x ~1.15 (SEMI's 2028 WFE growth), below the $55.5B consensus

FQ3 FCF was $2.33B on $9.12B (25.6%, 83% of non-GAAP NI). 9M was only 51% of non-GAAP NI because of a $2.5B AR build and $1.99B capex. Consensus FY28 FCF of $13.97B on $55.5B is 25%. I take 22.5% because facilities capex for the doubled output capacity continues.

Judgment. Consistency check corrected by the citation gate 2026-10-15: at a 23x P/E the earnings yield is 4.35%, so 75-80% FCF conversion would mean a 3.3-3.5% FCF yield, not 3.0%. 3.0% at 23x corresponds to ~69% conversion, which matches this leg's own 22.5% FCF margin against a 32.5% net margin. In round 1 I used 2.6% on FY27; I raise it for the FY28 (later-cycle) base. See citation_audit.json agent_leg_issues.

bear.story: In mid/late 2027 memory or AI-capex digestion starts, or customers flag a 2028 pause as the doubled output capacity lands. China weakens further: the BIS Affiliates Rule returns after the 2027-01-10 truce deadline (the company's own ~$600M/yr estimate) or controls broaden. NTM EPS is cut toward ~$17-18 and the multiple goes to ~18-19x. Semicap has historically fallen 50%+ in real downturns (2008, 2022).

base.story: FY27 lands near the $18.4 consensus. The Street carries FY28 at ~$22-24 as SEMI's WFE path (+21.8% 2027, +14.1% 2028) plays out. The multiple on NTM compresses from ~28x on FY27 today to ~23x on FY28, plus net cash, for a modest gain from $512.

bull.story: AI buildout visibility extends into 2028-30. FY28 tracks at or above the $23.85 consensus (toward $26-27, the MS-type path), gross margin moves into the low 50s, FCF conversion normalises to ~85%, and the stock holds ~30x and breaks the $723 closing high.

thesis_break_reason: $335 is ~18x FY27 consensus ($18.43), ~15x my $22 FY28 EPS, and ~19% below the $415.38 September closing low (9/16), which came on sentiment alone. A close there would most likely mean the market is pricing an actual 2027-28 WFE downturn: customer capex cuts at the TSMC/Micron/Samsung prints, an AMAT guide-down in Nov or Feb, or the BIS Affiliates Rule returning after the 2027-01-10 deadline with broader China restrictions. The ordinary 60%-vol swings seen in this cycle have not reached that level.

reasoning: Round 2 revision. The supervisor showed that my FY28 EPS input ($21.0) sat 12% below consensus without an explicit justification. I verified MarketScreener directly: FY27 is $18.43 EPS on $46.17B, and FY28 is $23.85 on $55.52B with $13.97B FCF. I now anchor on consensus and apply an explicit, smaller haircut to $22.0. The reason: consensus FY28 revenue of +20% outruns SEMI's July-2026 forecast of +14.1% WFE in 2028, and I accept the supervisor's correction that SEMI has 2027 at +21.8%. I also corrected net cash from ~$4 to ~$8/share (I had wrongly excluded ~$2.8B of LT fixed income) and shares to ~790M (buybacks slowed to $400M in FQ3). I disagree with the supervisor's implied 24x-on-corrected-EPS arithmetic ($545-580) and move to 23x instead of keeping 24x: the horizon multiple applies to FY28, which is visibly later in the cycle. The fair value rises from $494 to $513, about at spot. Scenarios: bear $330 (27%), base $550 (47%, up from $530), bull $820 (26%). Their lognormal mixture gives a median ~$525 and a mean ~$560, with left-tail mass kept for a semicap downturn and the Jan-10-2027 China policy binary. P(>=512) rises from 0.525 to 0.56. That is slightly above the supervisor's 0.535 because my base case includes net cash and a modest drift, but still close to a coin flip, because the outcome is mostly a multiple call. I also fixed facts: the closing high is $723.00 (intraday $739.67) and the September closing low is $415.38. Research was limited to two confirmatory checks (MarketScreener consensus, Micron capex guidance). The Micron FQ4 results were not yet available.
